source_evidence.observation: The exercise asks the reader to prove the equivalence of properties (a)--(d) in Proposition 2.7.1 by modifying the proof of Proposition 2.5.2.
For a random variable X, properties (a)--(d) are asserted to be equivalent, with positive parameters K_i that differ by at most an absolute constant factor.

The quantitative meaning of equivalence is that there is one absolute constant C such that, for any i,j in {1,2,3,4}, property i with parameter K_i implies property j with a parameter K_j satisfying K_j <= C K_i.
Property (a) is the tail bound P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t/K_1) for every t >= 0.
Property (b) is the moment bound ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K_2 p for every p >= 1.
Property (c) is the absolute-value MGF bound E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) for every lambda satisfying 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3.
Property (d) is the one-point exponential-moment bound E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2.

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.7.1 paragraph beginning 'Moreover, if E X = 0'
source_evidence.observation: The centering assumption E X = 0 belongs only to the additional equivalence with property (e); it is not an assumption for the equivalence of (a)--(d) requested in Exercise 2.7.2.

The proof that Exercise 2.7.2 directs the reader to modify forms a complete implication cycle: tail-to-moment uses the integral identity and a Gamma estimate; moment-to-exponential-MGF uses the exponential series, moment bounds, Stirling, and a geometric-series estimate; the next implication is immediate after parameter choice; and exponential-moment-to-tail uses Markov's inequality.

binders: X, a random variable. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Proposition 2.7.1 opening sentence]
For each property (a), (b), (c), and (d), a positive scale parameter K_1, K_2, K_3, or K_4, respectively. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Proposition 2.7.1 opening sentence and footnote 7]
conclusions: Prove that properties (a), (b), (c), and (d) of Proposition 2.7.1 are mutually equivalent. [PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2]

Prove the quantitative form of the equivalence: there is an absolute C such that every property i in {a,b,c,d}, with scale K_i, yields every property j in {a,b,c,d} with a scale K_j <= C K_i. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, footnote 7]

Obtain the equivalence by adapting the implication methods in the proof of Proposition 2.5.2 to exponential rather than sub-gaussian tails and moments. [PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2; PDF pages 13--14; printed pages 24--25, proof of Proposition 2.5.2]
definitions_and_conventions: Property (a): P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t/K_1) for all t >= 0. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(a)]
Property (b): ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K_2 p for all p >= 1. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(b)]
Property (c): E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) for all 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(c)]
Property (d): E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(d)]
'Differ by at most an absolute constant factor' means a uniform implication bound K_j <= C K_i for every ordered pair of the four properties. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, footnote 7]
implicit_context: Each K_i is strictly positive, so 1/K_i and the associated rescalings are defined. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Proposition 2.7.1 opening sentence]
The variables t, p, and lambda range over the full domains printed in their respective properties: t >= 0, p >= 1, and 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(a)--(c)]
The constant C is absolute: it is not allowed to depend on X, the selected pair of properties, or their scale witnesses. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, footnote 7]

No mean-zero condition is imposed for (a)--(d); E X = 0 is introduced only for the additional property (e), which Exercise 2.7.2 does not ask to include. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, paragraph after property (d); PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2]

details: The assertion is uniform over random variables X and is an equivalence of four existence-of-scale properties, not a claim that the same numerical K works unchanged in every property. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Proposition 2.7.1 opening sentence and footnote 7]
Within each property, its displayed inequality must hold for every value in the displayed t-, p-, or lambda-domain. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(a)--(c)]
The tail exponent is linear, -t/K_1, rather than quadratic. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(a)]
The L^p norm grows at most linearly in p, with scale K_2. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(b)]
Both (c) and (d) apply the exponential to |X|, so they are insensitive to the sign of X. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(c)--(d)]
Property (c) is only required for nonnegative lambda up to 1/K_3; it is not a two-sided MGF condition on X. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(c)]
Property (d) fixes the comparison value at 2. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(d)]
The exercise explicitly calls for modifying the proof of Proposition 2.5.2. [PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2]

For the corresponding first four sub-gaussian properties, that proof uses the cycle tail => moments => exponential moment => one-point exponential moment => tail, with layer-cake/Gamma, Taylor/Stirling/geometric-series, parameter selection, and Markov steps. [PDF pages 13--14; printed pages 24--25, proof of Proposition 2.5.2]

undebatable_constraints: The target is equivalence of exactly properties (a)--(d), not the centered property (e). [PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2]
The equivalence must preserve scale up to one absolute constant factor in the precise sense of footnote 7. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, footnote 7]
Property (a) has 2 exp(-t/K_1), with all t >= 0. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(a)]
Property (b) has ||X||_{L^p} <= K_2 p, with all p >= 1. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(b)]
Property (c) uses E exp(lambda |X|), the upper bound exp(K_3 lambda), and only 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(c)]
Property (d) uses E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2. [PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(d)]

No independence, symmetry, or centering hypothesis may be added to the equivalence of (a)--(d), since Proposition 2.7.1 assumes only that X is a random variable before stating those four equivalent properties. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Proposition 2.7.1 opening; PDF page 21; printed page 32, centered extension after (d)]
The requested proof is to be obtained by modifying the proof of Proposition 2.5.2. [PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2]

contracts.contract_plain_english: For an arbitrary random variable X, show that exponential tail decay, linear growth of all L^p norms, a small-nonnegative-parameter exponential-moment bound for |X|, and a one-point exponential-moment bound for |X| are all equivalent. The equivalence is quantitative: changing from any one property to any other may enlarge its positive scale only by a universal constant factor. No mean-zero assumption is part of this exercise, and property (e) is excluded. The intended proof adapts the first-four-property implication cycle in Proposition 2.5.2. [PDF page 20; printed page 31, Proposition 2.7.1 and footnote 7; PDF page 21; printed page 32, properties (a)--(d); PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.2; PDF pages 13--14; printed pages 24--25, proof of Proposition 2.5.2]
